technique.name: Declared utterances (rules)
technique.what: Route by token overlap with the sentences each SKILL.md declares — no model.

decision.note: Significantly worse than the model planner on fresh held-out (+4/−18, p=0.004).

technique.name: Selection by judgment (typed questions)
technique.what: A calibrated judge answers typed questions (choice over skills + none/clarify/several, fit yes-no per skill) instead of the planner choosing a tool.

technique.name: Ontology narrows, judge picks
technique.what: The request is grounded in the domain lexicon; skills covering the grounded classes (minus exclusions) are the judge's slate.

decision.note: Significantly worse than the judge alone on fresh 2 and 3 (0 fixed, 8 and 7 broken).

technique.name: Ontology alone (no model)
technique.what: Grounding + coverage/exclusion rule decides alone; no model call.

decision.note: Significantly worse than the judge alone (−12, −7).

technique.name: Ontology proposes, excludes veto, judge decides
technique.what: Recall-first proposal from grounding (direct → neighbourhood → catalog), excluded classes veto, the judge decides among the proposed.

decision.note: No gain over the judge (+0/−2); the veto by word match retired (spec 416 W1).

technique.name: Conformal acceptance
technique.what: Temperature-scaled judge distribution + a conformal prediction set: one skill routes, several asks, none declines.

decision.note: Coverage holds on both judges; no selection change at this set size — kept available as an acceptance mode, not the default.

technique.name: Fast skill stage before the planner
technique.what: One light-model call over the typed reading and ontology skill cards picks first; 'none' hands the ask to the planner over the other tools.

decision.note: Tokens to pick −86–90% on every comparison, better on fresh 5 (+7/−0); SKILL_SELECTION_DEFAULT=fast on faithnet. Watch: time to pick is higher than the planner-only pick.

technique.name: Lighter answer model
technique.what: The instruction skill answers with the provider's light model instead of the default.

decision.note: Faster (ask −20–34%) but the default answer was preferred side by side on fresh 4 (14 vs 6).

technique.name: The asker's context in the reading
technique.what: The judge is told the asker's recent skills and memory tags (seeded starting states), not only their standing.

decision.note: Context-dependent routing +11/−0 (p=0.001) at no token cost; live history behind SKILL_SELECTION_ASKER_CONTEXT=full (real asks only).

technique.name: Outcome-directed intent (chains by dataflow)
technique.what: The judge picks the outcome; a rule over produces/consumes builds the chain, prunes held inputs, names missing ones.

comparisons.note: with D4 (necessity + office prior) on both

decision.note: Full outcome reading pooled over 3 sets: +9/−10 at +169% pick tokens — superseded by selective outcome reading.

comparisons.note: with D4 (necessity + office prior) on both

technique.name: Whose it is decides the arrow
technique.what: An arrow whose ends are both party-qualified is decided by rule (our own scorecard never feeds a grantee's diligence) — no question asked.

decision.note: Same plan quality (33/36 both) at −12% tokens to pick; stays on in the outcome arm.

technique.name: Required vs enriching inputs; chain only on declared absence
technique.source: held-out 8 (development): 4 needless chain steps where an enriching input was merely unmentioned
technique.what: Every consumed slot is required or enriching; an enriching input is produced by a chain only when the request says it is absent — one yes-no per producible enriching class.

decision.note: In the FULL outcome reading, pooled +11/−16 (3 repeats on fresh 9 + 1) at +19% pick tokens: kept off there. Its absence question survives inside selective outcome reading, which is measured on its own.

technique.name: The asker's office as a prior (memory → role → typical capabilities)
technique.source: Offices typicallyUses in the domain ontology; held-out 8 office cases missed by both arms
technique.what: The asker's memory tags grounded in role classes; the reading names the office and the capabilities it typically uses.

decision.note: No gain on either arm (outcome −1, one-skill −1 net); declines rose on the office cases. Not adopted; the prompt wording is the suspect.

technique.name: Selective outcome reading (dataflow questions only when the pick has a producible input)
technique.source: The ledger: full outcome reading paid +124–174% pick tokens on every ask for chains that mattered in a handful of cases
technique.what: The cheap one-skill pick first; one small dataflow call only when the picked skill has an input another skill can produce (after the party rule) that the asker does not hold — about that skill's inputs only. Classes named with their lexicon glosses.

comparisons.note: vs the full outcome reading (glossed) — fresh 8 is development data for D4

decision.note: Pooled over six sets vs one-skill: +12/−2 (p=0.013), pick tokens −1%, ask −5%; regression panel fresh 4/5/6 no set worse (+0/−0, +3/−2, +2/−0). SKILL_SELECTION_DEFAULT=selective on faithnet. Live: a declared-absent inventory chains assessor → incident playbook. Watch: a chain with answers on runs ~29 s (two ~14 s skill answers in sequence).

comparisons.note: vs the full outcome reading (glossed) — fresh 8 is development data for D4

technique.name: The asker's records from the colo cache; the conversation write after the reply
technique.source: LLMCompiler (arXiv 2312.04511) scheduling; our stage marks (pre-run ~1.3 s, post-run ~2 s)
technique.what: ops/records=cached: the asker's conversation/facts/preferences read from the colo cache (the canonical answer this Worker last wrote; the vault on a miss), 'what is waiting on you' memoised a minute, and the conversation write lands after the reply (read-your-writes through the cache).
technique.plannedAb: same set, sync vs async recording: p50/p95 ask ms and phase:post-run; plan-exact unchanged; zero replies citing an uncommitted run.

decision.note: fresh 9, run alone and interleaved, 76 pairs: ask p50 4.62 s → 1.71 s (−63%), p90 10.96 → 7.19 s; pre-run 1.50 → 0.08 s, post-run 1.52 → 0.17 s; plan quality unchanged (+1/−2). OPS_RECORDS_DEFAULT=cached on faithnet. Caveat: an ask landing in another colo within the seconds before the vault write lands reads the older conversation.

technique.name: Stable prompt prefix for provider caching
technique.source: Gemini implicit caching (90% discount on cached prefix)
technique.what: The judge's instructions and the skills' ontology result cards first, byte-stable; the typed reading last — so the prefix is served from the provider's cache.
technique.plannedAb: cachedIn tokens, pick ms, plan-exact unchanged — current vs reordered.

decision.note: Measured before building: implicit prefix caching hit 29 of 1,338 stored runs, only on the planner's 12–17k-token prompts; the judge's 1.5–5k-token prompts never hit. The judge's prefix is already byte-stable, so implicit caching cannot help it; explicit caching would save ≤ ~100 ms per ask — deprioritised.

technique.name: Two-sample agreement (confidence without logprobs)
technique.source: 'Two samples are enough' (OpenReview), CISC (ACL 2025), CP-Router
technique.what: The fast judge runs twice in parallel; the same skill stands, two different skills ask which (clarify), a skill vs none holds. No conformal threshold yet — agreement alone first.
technique.plannedAb: macro TA, hold rate and precision-at-coverage on collisions / near-negatives / clarify; pick tokens ×2, pick ms ~same.

decision.note: Pooled +6/−2 (p=0.29) at +100% pick tokens, +8% ask. Promising on the clarify-heavy set (fresh 5: +5/−2) — revisit with a clarify-focused held-out set before any default.

technique.name: Personalized PageRank over the ontology to narrow the cards
technique.source: HippoRAG 2 (ICML 2025); RAG-MCP (2505.03275)
technique.what: Seed at the grounded classes and the asker's context, spread over cluster/class/dataflow edges to the skills; the judge sees the top-k cards + none + collision partners.
technique.plannedAb: offline Recall@k of the gold skill (≥ 0.99 required), then live pick tokens and plan-exact, all vs top-4 vs top-6.

technique.name: Decision cache keyed by the typed reading
technique.source: Agentic Plan Caching (NeurIPS 2025): −50% cost, −27% latency
technique.what: The pick's answers cached by a canonical signature of the reading (grounded classes, party, held classes, recent-skill class); the chain rule re-runs on a hit; authority is always fresh.
technique.plannedAb: replay recorded runs: hit rate, plan-exact on hits vs misses, p50 pick ms.

technique.name: Independent chain steps in parallel
technique.source: LLMCompiler
technique.what: The dataflow graph is the dependency graph: producers with no edge between them run concurrently (e.g. two inputs of one outcome).
technique.plannedAb: p50 ask ms on chain cases with answers on; plan-exact unchanged.

technique.name: SHACL-validated skill output with one repair
technique.source: OntoLogX (2510.01409), VirtualSet (2607.18821)
technique.what: A skill's answer is checked against the shape of the class it produces; a failure gets one repair call. Structure, never permission.
technique.plannedAb: shape conformance rate, repair rate, pairwise answer preference.

technique.name: Declared preconditions with named failure reasons
technique.source: Palantir Action Types — submission criteria
technique.what: A SKILL.md declares preconditions over the asker's typed state (held classes, party, role); checked by rule before any model call, refusing with the named reason.
technique.plannedAb: a failing-precondition negative twin per skill: right refusal with the right reason (target 100%), tokens per refusal ≈ 0.

technique.name: Verified exemplars on skill cards
technique.source: Snowflake semantic views — verified queries; Agent Workflow Memory / ReasoningBank
technique.what: Adjudicated request→skill pairs (development split only) retrieved into the judge's prompt, including recorded failures as 'not X because …'.
technique.plannedAb: held-out top-1 and plan-exact on collisions/near-negatives, extra pick tokens — on vs off.

technique.name: Lazy ontology verbalization
technique.source: RelationalAI RAI_VERBALIZE_MODEL / RAI_EXPLAIN_CONCEPT; Palantir property scoping
technique.what: The judge gets short skill cards; a concept's full explanation (its rules, excludes, neighbours) is fetched only for the top candidates on a second, rare call.
technique.plannedAb: pick tokens, p50/p95 pick ms, plan-exact non-inferiority.

technique.name: Dry-run chains against a snapshot
technique.source: Palantir branching action types
technique.what: A chain runs end to end against a vault snapshot with external effects disabled, so each step's input/output is judged without side effects.
technique.plannedAb: step-level input/output correctness on the chain cases of held-out 7 and 8.

technique.name: Per-step argument correctness as its own metric
technique.source: SAP AI Agent Hub tool-call correctness; Salesforce Testing Center
technique.what: Each step's bound arguments (the material passed along a chain, held records named, missing classes asked) scored apart from the skill choice.
technique.plannedAb: binding-error rate vs selection-error rate on chain and held-input cases.

technique.name: Per-request T-box subsetting
technique.source: TrustGraph ontology_selector (top-k + superclass/domain-range closure); Stardog schema agent; metaphactory reduction/import semantics
technique.what: Embed classes/properties; per request take the top-k plus the closure over superclasses and the produces/consumes neighbours the dataflow rule needs; only that subset enters the judge's reading.
technique.plannedAb: held-out 7/8: plan-exact, chains, missing named; pick tokens; p50/p95 pick ms.

technique.name: Rejected candidates and distributions on the run's provenance
technique.source: TrustGraph tg:toolCandidate / tg:llmDurationMs
technique.what: Each selection records the candidates offered, the runner-up and the judge's distribution on the PROV record (not only on the reply) — retrieval failure vs judge failure becomes separable.
technique.plannedAb: share of wrong picks where gold was offered; no runtime cost (ms delta ≈ 0).

technique.name: Steps score against reference chains
technique.source: Ontotext graphrag-eval Steps Score
technique.what: Chain quality as exact match AND edit distance to the gold plan (from the A-box tests), reported beside plan-exact — partial credit for a chain one step off.
technique.plannedAb: measurement only: steps-score distribution per variant on held-out 7/8.

technique.name: Small reranker shortlist ahead of the judge
technique.source: TrustGraph (flashrank cross-encoder replaced LLM edge scoring)
technique.what: A cross-encoder/embedding reranker over skill cards shortlists the judge's options; the judge sees top-k + none + collision partners.
technique.plannedAb: Recall@k of gold (≥ 0.99), then pick tokens and plan-exact live.

technique.name: Faster vault operations (the ~1.5 s per verified call)
technique.source: Stage breakdown, fresh 9 (2026-09-27): pick ~1.2 s; read:asker-records 1.58 s, record:conversation 1.63 s, read:waiting 1.50 s — three vault operations are ~70% of a pick-only ask · Inside one vault call (demo-mcp tail, 2026-09-27, 4 calls): ~260 ms to the service-MAC accept, ~270 ms delegation verification (on-chain signature + revocation reads), ~170 ms delegation binding, ~350 ms the vault op — ~1.05 s, about half of it re-verifying a token the caller already reuses.
technique.what: Candidates, each with its security reasoning first (a spec, not a patch): (a) a verified-token cache keyed by the token digest with a revocation bound stated in seconds (weighs against per-step on-chain revocation — needs the authority doctrine's sign-off); (b) batch the post-run vault reads into one call; (c) move 'what is waiting' to the Home's own poll; (d) find the ~260 ms before the service-MAC accept.
technique.plannedAb: phase:pre-run and phase:post-run p50/p95 — vault as is vs the change; correctness: the next ask recalls this turn (a two-ask pronoun probe).

technique.name: Skill-answer latency (the ~14 s per applied skill)
technique.source: Live, 2026-09-27: a two-step chain ran 29 s of a 33 s ask — each skill.apply ~14 s; the lighter answer model was faster but lost side by side (14 vs 6)
technique.what: Candidates: stream the answer to the surface as it is produced (time to first words, not to the whole answer); cap the answer to what the skill's method needs; for a chain, stream the first step's result while the second runs; answer-model routing by skill (a light model only where side-by-side shows no loss).
technique.plannedAb: answers on: time to first token and whole-ask p50/p90, side-by-side preference vs the current answers — per skill.

technique.name: A chain's intermediate step produces only the typed artifact
technique.source: Live chain ran 29 s: two ~14 s skill answers in sequence; the intermediate step's reader is the next skill, not the person
technique.what: The producer step in a chain is asked for ONLY the class the next step consumes, as a compact working artifact, under a smaller token budget (600).

comparisons.note: answers on, rubric on the terminal skill

decision.note: Chain panel 1: on the chained runs ask p50 28.6 → 23.1 s (−19%), output tokens −44%, rubric 0.94 → 1.00 (the rubric saturates). Needs a side-by-side of the final answers before any default.

comparisons.note: answers on, rubric on the terminal skill

technique.name: Selective reading looks downstream of the pick
technique.source: Chain panel 1 (development): grant chains chained 2/24 — the pick lands on the FIRST skill named ('work out the deadline… and draft'), and selective reading looked only upstream
technique.what: When the picked skill produces a class another skill consumes (the party rule not refusing), one yes-no in the same small call: does the request also want that next result? If so the plan ends there.

decision.note: Pooled +5/−4 at +24% pick tokens, +32% ask time (chain panel 2: producer-first 4/14 → 6/14, controls unharmed; fresh 9 −2). The misses are mostly the TERMINAL skill picked without its upstream step — the absence question does not cover "make it as a step" phrasing. Next: widen that question (judged on chain panel 3).

technique.name: Absence question covers 'make it as a step'
technique.source: Chain panel 2 misses: 'take stock of every AI tool we use and then build the response plan' — the terminal skill picked, the inventory step not added
technique.what: The enriching-input question also counts a request that ASKS for the input to be made first ('take stock… then', 'list the deadlines and…') — not only one saying it is missing.

decision.note: Pooled +0/−3: chains asked as a step stayed 1/12 either way; the misses were the pick landing on the first OR the last step — not wording.

technique.name: Plan choice: the rule enumerates the plans around the pick, the judge picks one
technique.source: Chain panels 1–3 (development): yes-no questions around a single pick failed both ways — the pick lands on the first step as often as the last
technique.what: For a pick with dataflow arrows, the ontology enumerates the few allowed plans (alone · producer → pick · pick → consumer; party rule applied, held inputs pruned) and one choice question picks the plan. No call for a pick with no arrows.

decision.note: Chain panel 4 (judging): chains 4/16 → 16/16, all 12 controls intact (+12/−0, p=0.0005). Regression fresh 8/9 not significantly worse (+3/−7 raw; 4 of the 7 were the FIRST-stage pick declining below the floor at p≈0.43, identical code before plan choice — noise; 2 real over-extensions: assess → incident on "gap roadmap" / "ready for new AI rules"). Cost: +22% ask, +21% pick tokens. SKILL_SELECTION_PLAN=choice on faithnet.

technique.name: A second sample only for a borderline first pick
technique.source: fresh 9 plan-choice run: the first-stage pick declined 4× at top p ≈ 0.43 where a rerun gave 0.68–1.0 — and a declined real ask reaches the planner WITHOUT the skills ("can't help")
technique.what: When the fast pick's top probability lands in a borderline band (e.g. 0.35–0.6), one more sample; the mean decides. Two-sample agreement always cost 2× tokens; this pays only on the borderline.
technique.plannedAb: instability (same case, repeated) and hold rate on positives; pick tokens should rise only on the borderline share.

decision.note: Pooled +5/−5 (fresh 8 + 6, ×2); declined positives 8/132 → 6/132; instability unchanged; pick tokens −0.1% — the band [0.35, 0.6] almost never fired, so first-pick variance mostly lies outside it. Next look: which declines are genuine abstentions vs variance (repeat-level analysis on the full ledger).

rule: Quality moves when the paired McNemar test gives p < 0.05 (else "same"). Cost moves when the paired bootstrap 95% interval of the median change in tokens-to-pick or the ask's time excludes 0 AND the change is at least 10%. The row's verdict is the latest comparison's; "inconclusive" when fewer than 8 paired cases.
